clarity_findings.claim: The bulleted list under "Which buildings mobilize:" mixes buildings that DO mobilize with entries that don't.
clarity_findings.problem: Of the five bullets, the first three (finished, damaged, upgrading/repairing) are things that DO mobilize workforce, but the fourth ("A building under construction mobilizes nothing until it is finished") is the opposite case, and the fifth ("Demolishing a building frees its workforce at once") is an action, not a building state. A reader skimming the "Which buildings mobilize:" header may misread the last two bullets as further examples of mobilizing buildings before catching the reversal.
clarity_findings.fix: Split the list, or add a short lead-in clause to the last two bullets (e.g. "Exceptions:") so the header's promise ("which buildings mobilize") isn't contradicted by list items that describe the opposite.

clarity_findings.claim: The over-mobilization block gives the worked example before the general formula.
clarity_findings.problem: "12 workforce, 15 mobilized: outputs reduced by 20 %" appears above "penalty = 1 − workforce ÷ mobilized", so the reader sees concrete numbers before the rule that produced them, then has to map back once the abstract formula appears.
clarity_findings.fix: Swap the two lines (formula first, then the worked example), matching the example-explains-the-formula flow used elsewhere in the manual.

votes.reason: The definition, mobilization rules, and over-mobilization formula are all concrete and given with a worked example, but the first screenshot creates a small label mismatch a new player has to puzzle out.
stumbles: The screenshot is titled "POPULATION" yet the highlighted stat is "2/15" workforce (mobilized/total) — a player has to infer that this box's first number is workforce, not population itself, even though the text above says "Workforce is a system's population rounded down to whole points."
"penalty = 1 − workforce ÷ mobilized" requires mapping back to the "12 workforce, 15 mobilized" line above it to see which number goes where — a brief re-read to confirm 1 − 12/15 = 20%.

"Each building mobilizes a fixed workforce, the same at every level" is asserted but the accompanying building-card screenshot only shows level 1 selected, so it doesn't visually demonstrate the "same at every level" claim.

votes.reason: The core rule and the over-mobilization formula are stated with a clean worked example, but the page swaps between "workforce" and "population" terminology at two points, forcing a quick double-check.
stumbles: "Tooltips show it as Over-mobilized population." — switches to "population" right after several paragraphs all using "workforce," making a skimmer pause to confirm it's the same stat.

The system-population shot is captioned "Mobilized workforce and total workforce" but sits under a box header reading "POPULATION" showing "2/15" next to a person icon — reads like a population count, not a workforce figure, until you connect it back to the caption.

"Workforce is a system's population rounded down to whole points" then "Buildings mobilize part of it" — "it" needs a beat to resolve to workforce rather than population, since the two are introduced almost as synonyms.
